deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page is part of Grothendieck's notes for a talk on crystals. Section 4 of the outline on the previous page is 'the idea of the Gauss–Manin connection'. Here he recalls Manin's 1958 work and then sketches an elementary construction of the Gauss–Manin connection.

(1) Manin's setting. k is a field of characteristic 0 and K/k a function field. Derivations of K/k act on de Rham cohomology. In Grothendieck's words this gives an integrable connection on H^*, though Manin does not use geometric language. For H^1, when K is the function field of a smooth proper variety over a field with derivations (the 'X' of the next line), Manin proves, in a rather complicated way, a stability statement. The subspace H^1(X,Ω^•) of H^1_DR of the function field is stable under the operators θ_x. Concretely: the de Rham H^1 of the proper smooth model is the space of differentials of the second kind modulo exact differentials, and differentiating a second-kind class along a base derivation stays of the second kind.

(2) §3.5, the simple direct argument. Let f: X→S and let ξ be a derivation of O_S. Suppose ξ lifts locally over S to a derivation ξ̄ of O_X compatible with ξ. This holds if X is formally smooth and affine over S.
- The Lie derivative θ_ξ̄ = d i_ξ̄ + i_ξ̄ d acts on absolute forms.
- It preserves the ideal generated by f^*Ω^1_S, so it descends to Ω^•_{X/S}.
- There it gives a ξ-semilinear endomorphism of f_*Ω^•_{X/S} commuting with d.
- Two lifts differ by a vertical field η. On relative forms θ_η = d i_η + i_η d (Cartan's homotopy formula), so θ_η is null-homotopic. Hence the action is independent of the lift up to homotopy, and depends only on ξ.
- With X affine over S, H^i(f_*Ω^•_{X/S}) = R^i f_*Ω^•_{X/S}. Derivations of S therefore act on these modules.
- O_S-linearity in ξ: lift aξ by f^*(a)ξ̄. Then θ_{aξ̄}ω = aθ_ξ̄ω + da∧i_ξ̄ω, and da = 0 in Ω_{X/S}.
- Compatibility with brackets: [θ_ξ̄, θ_η̄] = θ_[ξ̄,η̄], and [ξ̄,η̄] lifts [ξ,η].
- So if S is smooth over T, f_*Ω^•_{X/S} and the R^i f_* carry an integrable connection relative to T. This is the Gauss–Manin connection.

(3) The next page, (ii), globalises the construction for f smooth and quasi-projective (presumably by Čech gluing with homotopies; an appendix is cited). It yields a canonical absolute connection on Rf_*Ω^•_{X/S} in the derived-category sense. Grothendieck worries that this does not automatically give connections on each R^i individually, especially in characteristic p.
errors: Not an error, but a gap: the identification H^i(f_*Ω^•_{X/S}) = R^i f_*Ω^•_{X/S} needs X affine over S. Without it one must glue local lifts with homotopies (Čech), which is deferred to (ii) and an appendix.

Integrability (compatibility with brackets) is called trivial. At the level of complexes it does hold on the nose, since [θ_ξ̄, θ_η̄] = θ_[ξ̄,η̄]. In the non-affine glued situation the compatibility holds only up to coherent homotopy, so it is not trivial there.

Next page (context): the doubt that the R^i f_* get connections individually in characteristic p turned out to be unfounded. Katz–Oda (1968) construct an integrable Gauss–Manin connection on each R^i f_* for f smooth and S smooth over T, in any characteristic.

ideas.what: Interpretation of Manin's 1958 derivation action on de Rham cohomology of function fields as an integrable connection on H^*, and of the second-kind stability as a Gauss–Manin statement
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (IHES notes 1966, in Dix exposés 1968) discusses the Gauss–Manin connection and its crystalline origin

ideas.what: Construction of the Gauss–Manin connection by lifting base derivations to Lie derivatives on the total space; independence of the lift via Cartan's homotopy formula; linearity and bracket compatibility
ideas.modern_name: Lie-derivative / Cartan-homotopy description of the Gauss–Manin connection
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; Katz–Oda (1968) and Katz's later explicit Čech descriptions; Lie-derivative description standard in Hodge theory (Griffiths, Voisin)
ideas.where_published: possibly sketched in the Crystals lectures; unsure

ideas.what: Canonical connection on Rf_*Ω^•_{X/S} as an object of the derived category, as distinct from connections on individual cohomology sheaves (next page)
ideas.modern_name: Gauss–Manin connection at the derived / D-module level (∫_f of O_X)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Katz–Oda; later D-module theory (Bernstein, Kashiwara, Laumon)

missed.claim: Grothendieck had, by 1966–67, the elementary Cartan-homotopy proof of existence and integrability of the Gauss–Manin connection, plus a derived-category version, apparently before or contemporaneous with Katz–Oda (1968). This is a minor priority/attribution point; the method itself became folklore.
missed.quote: En fait, par des arguments très simples directs, reposant sur la "formule d'homotopie" de Cartan d i_x + i_x d = θ_x on peut montrer...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical credit only. The construction is standard today.

deep.surprise_reason: Clean early sketch of the Lie-derivative construction of Gauss–Manin. Mathematically this is folklore and is essentially in Katz–Oda, so it adds little beyond a modest priority note.
transcription_corrections: 'H^1(X, Ω^•_{X/k}) (qui est ⊂ H^1_DR(K/k))' is the hypercohomology de Rham H^1 of the smooth proper model (second-kind differentials mod exact), viewed inside the de Rham H^1 of the function field. The relative subscript should probably be over the field of constants, not literally k.
'[-K est-] provient d'une variété propre lisse': the crossed-out letter is 'K'. The phrase means 'when K comes from a proper smooth variety'.

The boxed marginal insert read as '{+différentiellement d'affine [?]+}' plausibly reads 'si f formell. lisse et affine', or similar. The main sentence reads 'dont dépend seulement de ξ' (the homotopy class depends only on ξ).
'ce compatible [?] à la loi de linéarité et des crochets' probably reads 'de façon compatible à la loi de linéarité et des crochets'.
The last line begins with 'crochets trivialement' (continuing the previous line), followed by 'donne pour f_*(Ω^•_{X/S}) et sur les R^if_*(Ω^•_{X/S}) une conn. intégrable rel/T'.
